topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course structure, sets out the core theme of cancer causation, and outlines the key learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Foundations of Cancer Causation: Intrinsic Mutations, Environment, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the core nature of cancer as a genetic and microenvironmental disease, examining the balance between intrinsic random mutation and environmental exposures through public debates and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Pathogens and Infectious Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological pathogens contribute to oncogenesis, surveying various cancer-associated infectious agents and detailing the epidemiological and molecular mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens and Metabolic Bioactivation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how specific dietary, environmental, and tobacco-derived mutagens and radiation cause DNA damage, detailing the endogenous metabolic pathways that bioactivate these compounds into reactive mutagens.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic factors like chronic inflammation drive tumor promotion, detail the classical two-stage model of carcinogenesis, and explore how host tissue developmental state influences susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the analytical, epidemiological, and experimental methods used to determine and validate carcinogenicity, ranging from mutational signature sequencing and biobanks to animal models and in vitro Ames assays.
